claims.text: A controlled aging heat treatment will induce uniformly distributed nanoscale coherent precipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Formation of uniformly distributed nanoscale coherent precipitates will improve the alloy's strength–plasticity balance relative to the untreated single-phase alloy.
The starting refractory high-entropy alloy is in an as-cast or solution-treated, single-phase homogeneous state.
A tailored aging heat treatment promotes nucleation and growth of nanoscale coherent precipitates.
The alloy composition must support formation of the desired precipitate phase.
Aging temperature and duration must be optimized to obtain a uniform nanoscale precipitate dispersion.
The aging treatment must avoid excessive precipitate coarsening and phase segregation.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Precipitate coherency facilitates dislocation nucleation and dynamic recovery.
Facilitated dislocation nucleation and dynamic recovery maintain or improve ductility.
The aged alloy will exhibit a statistically significant increase in yield strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The aged alloy will exhibit improved plastic-strain capacity relative to the untreated alloy.
The strength–plasticity benefit is contingent on achieving a uniform nanoscale precipitate distribution.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency may prevent the expected strength–plasticity benefit.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the predicted benefit is conditional on successfully obtaining uniform coherent nanoscale precipitates, but the falsification rule treats absence or coarsening of those precipitates as falsification. Failure to realize the stipulated mediator would ordinarily show an unsuccessful intervention rather than decisively refute the conditional mechanism.
